title: AI Agents List [2026] | Frameworks, Agentic Harnesses & Useful Repos
gist: A community-curated September 2026 directory of open-source agent frameworks, coding-agent harnesses, browser/voice agents and supporting infra, showing the market consolidating around big-lab SDKs and CLIs (OpenAI, Google, Microsoft, Anthropic) plus a few independents (Pydantic AI, LangGraph, OpenCode, Pi, Hermes), while notable earlier projects (AutoGen, Continue, Flowise, Roo Code) have been archived or put into maintenance mode. The recurring message is that the harness, permissions, licensing and supply-chain security now matter as much as the model.

insights.claim: Microsoft has put AutoGen into maintenance mode and now directs new users to Microsoft Agent Framework (Python and .NET, with workflow state, approvals and telemetry), consolidating its multi-agent efforts under one enterprise-oriented product.
insights.speaker: tegridydev
insights.so_what: Enterprise agent development on the Microsoft stack is converging on a single first-party framework, strengthening Microsoft's lock-in in Python/.NET shops.

insights.claim: Several once-popular open-source agent tools have stopped development: Continue says it is no longer actively maintained after a final 2.0.0 release, Flowise is archived, and the Roo Code extension shut down on 15 May.
insights.speaker: tegridydev
insights.so_what: The agent-tooling layer is churning fast; independent open-source projects without a funding/commercial path are dying, which favors big-lab and well-funded vendors.
insights.quote: Archived. Its README says the extension shut down on 15 May and points users towards alternatives.

insights.claim: LlamaIndex's own README says the company's focus has shifted towards document parsing and extraction, signalling a pivot away from the general-purpose RAG/agent framework it was known for.
insights.speaker: tegridydev
insights.so_what: Framework vendors are retreating to narrower monetizable niches (document parsing), suggesting generic orchestration frameworks are hard to monetize.
insights.quote: The current README says the company's focus has shifted towards parsing and extraction.

insights.claim: Every major AI lab now ships its own agent SDK and terminal coding agent: OpenAI (Agents SDK, Codex CLI), Google (ADK, Gemini CLI), Microsoft (Agent Framework), Anthropic (Claude Code, Claude Agent SDK), plus Qwen Code, ByteDance's DeerFlow and Nous Research's Hermes Agent.
insights.speaker: tegridydev
insights.so_what: Model providers are vertically integrating into the harness layer to capture developer workflow and token demand, squeezing independent framework startups.

insights.claim: The author's quick-pick shortlist for 2026 names Pydantic AI (typed Python agents), LangGraph (stateful workflows), smolagents (code agents), Mastra or VoltAgent (TypeScript), Codex CLI or OpenCode (terminal coding), Pi (extensible harness), Hermes Agent (memory assistant), GPT Researcher, Browser Use or Stagehand, and LiveKit Agents or Pipecat (voice) as the default starting points.
insights.speaker: tegridydev
insights.so_what: A mindshare map of which open-source projects are winning developer adoption per use case.

insights.claim: The agent 'harness' (execution loop, tools, context handling, sessions, errors, permissions) is framed as a distinct layer from the model: the model is the engine and the harness supplies the controls, making it a separate competitive surface.
insights.speaker: tegridydev
insights.so_what: Value capture is shifting to the harness/orchestration layer, where differentiation (and lock-in) can persist even as models commoditize.
insights.quote: Think of the model as the engine. The harness supplies the controls and connects it to the rest of the machine.

insights.claim: A new tier of prebuilt long-running agent harnesses has emerged on top of frameworks: Deep Agents (built on LangGraph), Pydantic AI Harness, Strands Agents, Letta Code and ByteDance's DeerFlow v2 all bundle planning, subagents, memory and persistence.
insights.speaker: tegridydev
insights.so_what: Framework vendors are moving up-stack to productize long-running autonomous agents, the likely next monetization battleground.

insights.claim: The author proposes evaluating harnesses on post-demo operational criteria: whether you can inspect a failed run, stop it, control its tools, resume work and measure its cost.
insights.speaker: tegridydev
insights.so_what: Observability, control and cost accounting are the enterprise buying criteria, favoring tracing/eval vendors like Langfuse and Promptfoo.
insights.quote: can you inspect a failed run, stop it, control its tools, resume work and measure what it cost?

insights.claim: Community feedback (LocalLLaMA) shows users split between Pi for its simplicity and extensibility and OpenCode, Codex, Cline or Hermes, with recurring complaints about context overhead, token costs and plugin bloat complicating local workflows.
insights.speaker: tegridydev
insights.so_what: There is no locked-in winner among coding harnesses; minimalism and token efficiency are competitive differentiators, keeping switching costs low.

insights.claim: Cline disclosed an unauthorised publication of its CLI package (version 2.3.0) on 17 February 2026, then issued a corrected release and changed its publishing process, a concrete supply-chain incident in a popular coding agent.
insights.speaker: tegridydev
insights.so_what: Coding agents with shell access are a live supply-chain attack vector, supporting demand for package integrity, sandboxing and agent-security tooling.

insights.claim: Many popular agent tools ship with permissive or absent guardrails: OpenCode's permissions mostly default to allow, Pi has no built-in filesystem/process/network/credential restrictions, Pydantic AI Harness's Coder runs unrestricted shell commands, and OpenClaw's main session tools run on the host unless sandboxing is configured.
insights.speaker: tegridydev
insights.so_what: Insecure defaults create a structural need for isolation and sandbox infrastructure (e.g. E2B) and enterprise-grade permission layers.
insights.quote: Its permission documentation says most permissions default to allowing actions, so configure these deliberately.
insights.locator: OpenCode: Coding agent with a terminal

insights.claim: Model Context Protocol's official server repository explicitly labels its reference implementations as educational examples, not production-ready, and protocol support (MCP, Agent Client Protocol, Agent2Agent) says nothing about whether a given plugin is trustworthy.
insights.speaker: tegridydev
insights.so_what: Interoperability standards are spreading faster than their security hardening, an opening for vetted MCP registries and agent-security vendors.
insights.quote: Protocol support does not tell you whether a particular plugin is trustworthy.

insights.claim: A wave of agent products are open-core or source-available rather than permissively open source: Dify uses a modified Apache licence restricting multi-tenancy and branding, n8n uses Sustainable Use/enterprise licences, AutoGPT's platform uses Polyform Shield, and Mastra and Langfuse carve out ee/ directories under enterprise terms.
insights.speaker: tegridydev
insights.so_what: Agent-tooling companies are monetizing via restrictive licences and enterprise carve-outs, a typical open-core business model worth tracking for revenue durability.
insights.quote: Do not describe it as ordinary permissive open source.

insights.claim: Anthropic's Claude Code is proprietary under commercial terms, and the MIT-licensed Claude Agent SDK bundles and depends on the separately governed Claude Code CLI, so building on it still ties developers to Anthropic's runtime.
insights.speaker: tegridydev
insights.so_what: Anthropic is keeping its core agent runtime closed while offering an open SDK wrapper, a lock-in strategy unlike OpenAI's Apache-licensed Codex CLI.

insights.claim: Many 'open' agent projects separate open repositories from hosted paid services, including Browser Use, Stagehand (Browserbase hosting), OpenHands, Kilo Code, VoltAgent (VoltOps) and GitLab Duo Agent Platform, whose public source does not make Duo functionality free to run.
insights.speaker: tegridydev
insights.so_what: Open-source repos serve as developer-acquisition funnels for hosted/cloud revenue; watch conversion to paid services as the monetization signal.
